introduction_markdown: Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section II in 1 1/2 hours; you are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section II, answer all questions choosing EITHER parts a, b and c OR parts d, e and f of each question. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Calculators are allowed.

figures.legende: Figure 3: a $4\,\Omega$ and a $6\,\Omega$ resistor in parallel, in series with a $2\,\Omega$ resistor, an instrument X and a $12\,\mathrm{V}$ cell; instrument Y is across the $2\,\Omega$ resistor

incertitudes: Pas de total imprimé par question : `points` de l'exercice = somme des marques imprimées (2 + 2 + 2).
Le corrigé suppose un ampèremètre et un voltmètre idéaux et une pile sans résistance interne (non indiquée par le sujet).

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the instruments labelled X and Y. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**X is an ammeter**: it is connected **in series** in the circuit and measures the current.

**Y is a voltmeter**: it is connected **in parallel** across the $2\,\Omega$ resistor and measures the potential difference across it.

questions.enonce_markdown: Calculate the total resistance of the circuit. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The ammeter has negligible resistance and the voltmeter draws negligible current, so only the three resistors count.

The $4\,\Omega$ and $6\,\Omega$ resistors are in parallel:

$R_p = \dfrac{4\times 6}{4+6} = \dfrac{24}{10} = 2.4\,\Omega$

This combination is in series with the $2\,\Omega$ resistor:

$R_T = 2.4 + 2 = 4.4\,\Omega$

questions.enonce_markdown: Calculate the current flowing through the $2\,\Omega$ resistor. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The $2\,\Omega$ resistor is in series with the rest of the circuit, so it carries the **total current** from the $12\,\mathrm{V}$ cell.

$I = \dfrac{V}{R_T} = \dfrac{12}{4.4} = 2.73 \approx 2.7\,\mathrm{A}$
